headline: Energy Surges on Middle East Tensions as Industrials Bear the Brunt of Earnings Disappointments
body_html:
Wednesday's midday tape is tilted lower in breadth — 300 names declining against 218 advancing across a 519-stock universe — yet the headline number obscures a sharp divergence in sector fortunes. Energy leads all groups, advancing nearly 1.8% as crude oil jumps close to 7% on escalating airstrikes in the Middle East and fresh signals that Iran will not permit regional oversight of the Hormuz Strait, tightening supply anxiety across global markets. Software ranks second with a gain of roughly 1.1%, lifted in part by a spectacular earnings-driven rally in Manhattan Associates, which has surged nearly 24% intraday.

The standout mover of the session, however, belongs to Verra Mobility, up an extraordinary 31.8% — the largest single-name gain in the universe mid-session. Garmin is also commanding attention, adding nearly 17% after what appears to be a well-received quarterly update. On the healthcare side, NeoGenomics and GE HealthCare are each posting double-digit advances, lending the sector a solid 0.6% gain.

The damage is concentrated in Industrials and Semiconductors, down 1.1% and 1.9% respectively. Lennox International has collapsed 17% and Vertiv Holdings shed more than 14%, suggesting earnings-driven re-ratings in HVAC and data-center infrastructure. Into the close, watch whether energy's geopolitical premium holds and whether Semiconductor weakness broadens.

briefs.headline: Crude Rockets Higher as Middle East Flashpoints Multiply
briefs.body: Oil is surging close to 7% on the session after fresh U.S. and Saudi strikes targeted Iran-backed fighters in Iraq and Iran explicitly ruled out any shared regional management of the Hormuz Strait. Reports of Houthi forces in Yemen contemplating transit fees in the Red Sea corridor are adding another layer of supply-route anxiety to an already tense market.

briefs.headline: Verra Mobility Vaults 32% on Midday Tape
briefs.body: Shares of Verra Mobility are the session's most dramatic mover, rallying nearly 32% intraday. The toll-technology and mobility-services company appears to have delivered results or guidance that caught the market off guard, pushing it to the top of the gainers board by a wide margin across the 519-name universe.

briefs.headline: Manhattan Associates Rockets After Supply-Chain Software Results
briefs.body: Manhattan Associates is up nearly 24% at midday, making it the second-largest gainer in the session. The supply-chain software specialist's quarterly report appears to have well exceeded expectations, propelling Software to the second-best sector performance of the day at a gain of roughly 1.1%.

briefs.headline: Lennox and Watsco Drag HVAC Names Sharply Lower
briefs.body: Lennox International is down 17.4% and peer distributor Watsco has shed 11.6%, suggesting the residential and commercial HVAC pocket of the market received a discouraging earnings signal. The paired decline is weighing on the broader Industrials sector, which is the second-worst performer on the day at minus 1.1%.

briefs.headline: Vertiv Slides 14% as Data-Center Infrastructure Stocks Face Scrutiny
briefs.body: Vertiv Holdings is off more than 14% in midday trading, the second-steepest decliner in the universe. The pullback in the data-center infrastructure name comes alongside broader Semiconductor weakness, raising questions about whether the capital-spending cycle underpinning AI infrastructure build-outs is running into near-term turbulence.

briefs.headline: Humana Holds Steady After Topping Quarterly Estimates
briefs.body: Humana posted results that exceeded analyst forecasts and reaffirmed its full-year profit outlook, citing medical costs that remained within projected ranges. The managed-care name is contributing to Healthcare's positive tone on the day, a sector that is advancing roughly 0.6% and benefiting additionally from double-digit gains in NeoGenomics and GE HealthCare.
